publish.title: Undo your last git commit: soft, mixed, hard, or revert
publish.description: Three ways to undo a commit with git reset, and when to use git revert instead.

scenes.headline: Undo your last commit
scenes.narration: You committed, and then spotted a mistake. Git gives you a few ways out, depending on what you want to keep.

scenes.headline: Keep the changes, undo the commit
scenes.narration: Reset soft moves the branch back one commit and keeps your changes staged, ready to commit again.

scenes.headline: Keep the files, unstage them
scenes.narration: A plain reset, which is mixed by default, also keeps your files but unstages them.

scenes.headline: The risky one
scenes.narration: The last option is the only one that destroys work, so read it twice before you run it.

scenes.headline: Throw it all away
scenes.narration: Reset hard discards the commit and your changes. Use it only when you are sure.

scenes.headline: Already pushed?
scenes.narration: If other people have your commit, do not rewrite history. Use git revert, which adds a new commit that undoes the old one.

scenes.headline: Pick the gentlest option
scenes.narration: Choose the gentlest option that does the job, and check git status afterwards.
